summary.title: Object-oriented programming
summary.one_liner: Learn when object-oriented design helps, how encapsulation works in Python, and how composition, inheritance, multiple inheritance, mix-ins and abstract classes differ.
takeaways: Encapsulation means data should be accessed through an object's methods; Python only enforces it by convention, using a leading underscore.
Composition models a has-a relationship by making objects attributes of other objects; aggregation is a weaker form without exclusive ownership.
Inheritance models an is-a relationship; use super() to call parent __init__ methods, including with multiple inheritance.
Mix-ins are small classes meant to add optional functionality through multiple inheritance, avoiding ambiguity such as the diamond problem.
Python can imitate abstract classes and interfaces by raising NotImplementedError in method definitions.
summary.summary: This chapter from a Python textbook explains why organising code into classes helps as programs grow, contrasting it with procedural code and global variables. It introduces encapsulation and the Python underscore convention, then covers composition (has-a) with a university course example and inheritance (is-a) with Person, Student and StaffMember classes. It continues with multiple inheritance, the diamond problem, mix-ins, and abstract classes or interfaces simulated with NotImplementedError. The page includes code examples and exercises on a music collection model and a custom exception hierarchy; the page text is cut off mid-example at the end.
